events.asset: DOJ criminal prosecutions of telehealth companies for controlled-substance distribution
events.title: DOJ charges a second telehealth company over controlled-substance prescribing
events.proposition: The Department of Justice announces criminal charges against a second telehealth or digital health company, or its executives, for unlawful distribution of controlled substances prescribed through the company's platform.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of a Department of Justice press release (justice.gov) announcing an indictment or criminal complaint against a telehealth or digital health company, or its executives, for unlawful distribution of controlled substances prescribed through the company's platform, in a case other than the Done case the author cites. The docket date of the charging document is the secondary source. Civil settlements, DEA administrative actions, state actions and cases against individual clinicians with no company platform do not count. FALSE when no such announcement has appeared by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: US Department of Justice press releases; federal court dockets (CourtListener) as a secondary source

readings: 'There's more coming' and 'first prosecution doesn't sound like last prosecution' read as at least one further criminal prosecution of the same kind: a company that prescribes controlled substances over the internet, charged with drug distribution.
court_outcome is the closest template for a federal enforcement action; the event resolves on the announcement of charges, not on a later verdict.

related_timeline.event: American Journal of Psychiatry publishes double-blind sham-controlled RCT of Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy (5-day accelerated iTBS) in treatment-resistant depression.
Colorado voters approve Proposition 122 (Natural Medicine Health Act), decriminalizing five plant psychedelics and authorizing regulated psilocybin healing centers.
DEA publishes proposed rules on telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances after the COVID PHE, including in-person visit requirements and 30-day limits.

related_timeline.event: Newsom vetoes SB 58, which would have decriminalized psilocybin and other plant psychedelics, citing the need for dosing and patient-protection guidelines first.

Venture studio Beckley Waves acquires ketamine telehealth company Nue Life after Nue Life's standalone model faltered.

events.asset: Prazosin (Minipress and generics) for PTSD or PTSD-associated nightmares
events.title: FDA approval of prazosin for PTSD or PTSD-associated nightmares
events.proposition: The FDA approves prazosin for post-traumatic stress disorder or for PTSD-associated nightmares, a new labeled indication for any prazosin product.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date the FDA approval letter or Drugs@FDA entry (or the sponsor's approval announcement) adds PTSD or PTSD-associated nightmares or sleep disturbance to the labeled indications of any prazosin product. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote or a filing acceptance is not an approval. Off-label use, a clinical guideline, a compendium listing or a VA/DoD recommendation is not an FDA label. A label limited to PTSD-associated nightmares counts, since the claim's context concerns nightmares. FALSE when no such indication appears on a prazosin label in Drugs@FDA by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA; sponsor press release as a secondary source

readings: 'an FDA label' = an FDA-approved indication on the prazosin label; PTSD or PTSD-associated nightmares both count.
'It' = prazosin (Minipress), the subject of the post; any prazosin product (brand or generic) counts.

related_timeline.key_number: 71.2% vs 47.6% no longer met PTSD criteria; remission 46.2% vs 21.4%

VA issues a request for applications to fund research on MDMA, psilocybin and other psychedelics for PTSD and depression, its first such funding in about six decades.

related_timeline.event: FDA accepts Lykos's NDA for midomafetamine (MDMA)-assisted therapy for PTSD with priority review; PDUFA date set for August 11, 2024.
ICER draft evidence report finds evidence on MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for PTSD insufficient because of functional unblinding and trial-conduct concerns.
FDA Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee votes against MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD, citing functional unblinding, missing safety data and site misconduct.
Advisory committee votes 2-9 that MDMA-assisted therapy is not shown effective for PTSD and 1-10 that benefits do not outweigh risks.
FDA issues a complete response letter (dated August 8) for MDMA capsules for PTSD, requesting an additional Phase 3 trial and citing safety and data-integrity concerns.

events.asset: Midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD: the Lykos Therapeutics NDA under FDA review in June 2024
events.title: FDA non-approval of the midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) NDA cites insufficient safety data
events.proposition: The FDA's action on the Lykos Therapeutics midomafetamine NDA under review in June 2024 informs the sponsor that the application lacks the safety data necessary for approval: a complete response letter or other written non-approval that cites insufficient safety data or requests additional safety data.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date the sponsor (Lykos Therapeutics) publicly discloses, or the FDA publicly states, that the FDA's action letter on the midomafetamine NDA under review on the statement date cites insufficient or missing safety data or requests additional safety data, alone or together with other deficiencies. FALSE on the date the FDA approves that NDA in the pending review cycle, on the date the sponsor's or the FDA's disclosed summary of the action letter names only deficiencies that do not concern safety data, or at the deadline when no FDA action letter on that NDA has been disclosed. A PDUFA date extension or a request for more review time is not the event. If the FDA has acted but neither the sponsor nor the FDA discloses the grounds within 12 months after the action, the event is unresolvable.

resolution_source.name: Lykos Therapeutics press releases and public statements describing the FDA action letter; FDA public statements as a secondary source

readings: 'inform the study sponsor that they don't have the safety data necessary to approve the drug' = an FDA action letter on the pending NDA that cites insufficient safety data or requests additional safety data; the post names EKG and laboratory data, but any safety-data deficiency counts.
A complete response letter is the usual form of such a letter; any written FDA non-approval communication that the sponsor discloses counts.
MDMA-assisted therapy, MDMA-AT and midomafetamine name the same asset.

events.asset: atai Life Sciences common stock (Nasdaq: ATAI, or its successor listing): market capitalization
events.title: atai Life Sciences market capitalization at or above US$10 billion
events.proposition: The market capitalization of atai Life Sciences (Nasdaq: ATAI, or its successor listing) is at or above US$10 billion at a market close, per Nasdaq closing price and shares outstanding in SEC filings.
events.criterion: Resolved on the named data series only: the market capitalization of atai Life Sciences (Nasdaq: ATAI, or its successor listing), computed as the Nasdaq closing share price multiplied by the shares outstanding stated on the cover page of atai's most recent periodic SEC filing on EDGAR. TRUE on the first trading day on which that closing market capitalization is at or above US$10 billion. The threshold is in the forecaster's words, so it resolves as binary at US$10 billion with no band. FALSE at the deadline when no market close has reached US$10 billion. If the shares stop trading with no successor listing and no price series has published 12 months after the deadline, the event is unresolvable. Realized values are stored, not scored.

resolution_source.name: Nasdaq closing price for ATAI and shares outstanding in atai Life Sciences periodic filings on SEC EDGAR

quantity.metric: Market capitalization of atai Life Sciences (Nasdaq: ATAI, or successor listing) at a market close
quantity.series: Nasdaq closing price of ATAI multiplied by shares outstanding on the cover page of atai's most recent periodic SEC filing (SEC EDGAR)

readings: 'double-, triple-digit billion-dollar company' = market capitalization of at least USD 10 billion; the range's lower bound is the threshold.

events.asset: Midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD: Lykos Therapeutics' appeal of the August 2024 complete response letter
events.title: FDA grants the Lykos appeal of the 2024 midomafetamine complete response letter
events.proposition: The FDA grants Lykos Therapeutics' request for reconsideration or formal dispute resolution appeal of the August 2024 complete response letter for midomafetamine for PTSD.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the FDA's written decision (or, if that letter is not public, the sponsor's public announcement of it) that grants the request for reconsideration or the formal dispute resolution appeal of the August 2024 complete response letter: the FDA withdraws its request for an additional Phase 3 trial or approves the NDA on the data already submitted. A meeting granted or held, a resubmission accepted for review, or an approval that follows a new Phase 3 trial does not count. If no reconsideration request or appeal is decided in the sponsor's favour by the end of the window, the event is FALSE.

resolution_source.name: Lykos Therapeutics press releases; FDA CDER formal dispute resolution decision letters

readings: 'An appeal' is read as the request for reconsideration that Lykos said it would make after the complete response letter (per the post), or a formal dispute resolution appeal; either route counts.
'Doomed to failure' is read as: the FDA does not grant the appeal. The event is written positively (the appeal is granted) and the forecaster denies it.
court_outcome is the closest template: an agency ruling on an administrative appeal. The event resolves on the decision on the appeal, not on a later approval after new trials.

events.asset: Acadia Healthcare involuntary psychiatric holds alleged in the New York Times investigation: criminal charges
events.entity: US Department of Justice or a state prosecutor (attorney general or district attorney)
events.title: Criminal charges over Acadia Healthcare involuntary psychiatric holds
events.proposition: A federal or state prosecutor files criminal charges against Acadia Healthcare or one or more of its current or former employees or executives over the involuntary psychiatric holds alleged in the New York Times investigation.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the first criminal indictment, information or complaint (or the date of the Department of Justice or state attorney general press release announcing the charges) that names Acadia Healthcare, a subsidiary, or a current or former Acadia employee or executive as a criminal defendant for conduct that includes holding psychiatric patients against their will or beyond medical necessity, as alleged in the New York Times investigation of Acadia Healthcare that the author discusses. A civil suit, a civil settlement, a CMS or state licensing action, a subpoena, or an announced investigation without charges does not count. FALSE when no such charge appears on a court docket or in a prosecutor's announcement by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Court dockets (CourtListener, PACER); DOJ and state attorney general press releases

readings: 'This' refers to the author's hope in the preceding paragraph: that the circumstances be investigated and, if substantiated, that every person involved face criminal charges. The coder resolves it on the filing of charges (the observable step); charges against any one person or the company count.
court_outcome is the closest template for a criminal enforcement action; the event resolves on the charge, not on a later verdict.

related_timeline.event: Colorado voters approve Proposition 122 (Natural Medicine Health Act), decriminalizing five plant psychedelics and authorizing regulated psilocybin healing centers.
Ketamine Wellness Centers, a Delic Holdings subsidiary, abruptly shuts all of its ketamine clinics across nine states.
FDA issues draft guidance 'Psychedelic Drugs: Considerations for Clinical Investigations' (docket FDA-2023-D-1987); comments due August 25, 2023.
Newsom vetoes SB 58, which would have decriminalized psilocybin and other plant psychedelics, citing the need for dosing and patient-protection guidelines first.
FDA warns patients and providers about risks of compounded ketamine products, including oral formulations used at home for psychiatric disorders via telemedicine.
VA issues a request for applications to fund research on MDMA, psilocybin and other psychedelics for PTSD and depression, its first such funding in about six decades.
FDA grants Breakthrough Therapy designation to MM120 (LSD D-tartrate) for generalized anxiety disorder.
EMA holds a multi-stakeholder workshop 'Psychedelics: towards an EU regulatory framework' on clinical development and access.
Done Global CEO Ruthia He and clinical president David Brody are arrested on federal charges over an alleged $100M Adderall telehealth distribution scheme.
VA awards up to $1.5M over five years for its first VA-funded psychedelic study: MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD and alcohol use disorder at Providence and West Haven VAs.
VA announces funding for its first study of MDMA-assisted therapy in decades, for veterans with PTSD and alcohol use disorder.
Departments announce they will not enforce the 2024 MHPAEA final rule's new requirements until the ERIC litigation ends plus 18 months; the 2013 rule and statute still apply.

events.asset: Acadia Healthcare involuntary psychiatric holds alleged in the New York Times investigation: litigation
events.entity: US federal or state courts (Acadia Healthcare as defendant)
events.title: Litigation filed over Acadia Healthcare involuntary psychiatric holds
events.proposition: A lawsuit or government enforcement action over the involuntary psychiatric holds alleged in the New York Times investigation is filed against Acadia Healthcare.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the first civil complaint (including a patient or shareholder class action) or government civil or criminal action filed on or after 2024-09-04 against Acadia Healthcare or a subsidiary, or the date of the Acadia Healthcare SEC filing that first discloses such an action, in which the allegations include holding psychiatric patients against their will or beyond medical necessity as described in the New York Times investigation the author discusses. Suits that do not allege that conduct (for example ordinary malpractice claims), suits filed before 2024-09-04, and subpoenas or investigations without a filed action do not count. FALSE when no such action has been filed or disclosed by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Court dockets (CourtListener, PACER); Acadia Healthcare SEC filings (legal proceedings)

readings: 'Litigation' is read as any filed civil or government action tied to the alleged involuntary holds; the author names no plaintiff type, so patient, shareholder and government actions all count.
'Will now ensue' is read as litigation not yet filed at the statement date; a suit filed before 2024-09-04 does not count.
company_event is used because the criterion resolves on a court filing or SEC disclosure about the company. The implied claim about profitability is not coded.
